Define a chromosome's inheritance or recombination rule

Source: R/define_chromosome.R
define_chromosome.Rd

Changes how one chromosome is passed on, for sex chromosomes (X/Y, Z/W, X0, Z0) and organelles (mitochondria, plastids). define_genome() starts every chromosome as a diploid autosome: one copy from each parent, recombining in both sexes. Call define_chromosome() after define_genome() and before add_founders(), once per rule that differs from that default.

Each call sets one of two things:

  • Inheritance: give from_parent_1 and from_parent_2, the number of copies an offspring inherits from its sire (parent 1) and its dam (parent 2), optionally for one offspring_sex. Writes chr_inheritance.

  • Recombination: give recombines, whether a parent recombines this chromosome when it makes gametes, optionally for one parent_sex. Writes chr_recombination.

They are separate calls because "which sex" means different animals: the offspring for inheritance, the parent for recombination.

Usage

define_chromosome(
  pop,
  chr_name,
  offspring_sex = NULL,
  parent_sex = NULL,
  line_name = NULL,
  from_parent_1 = NULL,
  from_parent_2 = NULL,
  recombines = NULL,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

pop

A tidybreed_pop with a genome from define_genome().

chr_name

Character scalar: a chromosome name from define_genome()'s chr_names (e.g. "X").

offspring_sex

Inheritance calls only: "M" or "F" for a rule that applies to offspring of that sex, or NULL (default) for both.

parent_sex

Recombination calls only: "M" or "F" for a rule that applies when a parent of that sex makes gametes, or NULL (default) for both.

line_name

Optional line name: the rule applies only to animals of that line (the offspring's line for inheritance, the parent's for recombination), for crossbreeding designs whose lines differ. NULL (default) applies to every line. A chromosome that any line's rule makes special is drawn on add_offspring()'s slower per-offspring path for every line.

from_parent_1, from_parent_2

Inheritance calls: whole numbers, always given together, of copies from the sire (parent 1) and the dam (parent 2). Their sum is 0, 1 or 2; see the table in Details.

recombines

Recombination calls: TRUE if the chromosome recombines when a parent makes gametes, FALSE if it is passed on whole (a Y, a W). To stop one sex recombining on every chromosome, use recombines_M / recombines_F in define_genome() instead.

overwrite

Logical. TRUE (default) replaces an existing rule with the same chromosome, sex and line. FALSE refuses instead, to guard against redefining a rule by accident. Every chromosome already has a default rule (both sexes, all lines) from define_genome(), so overwrite = FALSE is useful only for sex- or line-specific rules.

Value

The tidybreed_pop, invisibly. Assign it back.

Details

Copy counts are absolute numbers of copies, at most 2 in total:

Chromosomeoffspring_sexfrom_parent_1 (sire)from_parent_2 (dam)
Autosome (the default)either11
Mammalian X in males"M"01
Mammalian Y in males"M"10
Mammalian Y in females"F"00
Avian Z in females"F"10
Avian W in females"F"01
Avian W in males"M"00
Maternal mitochondriaeither (NULL)01

Only the sexes that differ from the default need a rule: a mammalian X in females keeps the default 1, 1. A chromosome a parent carries in one copy is passed on unchanged; one it carries in two copies recombines as chr_recombination says.

Which rule applies. For an animal of sex S in line L, the most specific stored rule wins: (S, L), then (S, any line), then (any sex, L), then the default (any sex, any line). Inheritance rules are looked up with the offspring's sex and line, recombination rules with the parent's.

Timing. Founders and offspring are written with the rules in force at the time, so set every inheritance rule before add_founders(). Once individuals exist, an inheritance call that would change the copies any of them carry is refused (nothing is written): their stored haplotypes would no longer match, and breeding from them would fail. A call that changes nothing for existing individuals, such as a rule for a line with no individuals yet, is still allowed. Recombination rules can be changed at any time; they apply to gametes made afterwards.

Every write is checked in the same transaction (one rule per key, both sexes resolvable, at most 2 copies); a rejected call leaves the previous rule in place. See the rules with get_table(pop, "chr_inheritance") and get_table(pop, "chr_recombination").

See also

define_genome(), add_founders(), add_offspring().

Examples

# Mammalian X and Y: inheritance for the sexes that differ, and a
# non-recombining Y
pop <- open_pop(pop_name = "mammal", db_name = ":memory:") |>
  define_genome(n_loci = 300, n_chr = 3, chr_len_Mb = 100,
                chr_names = c("1", "X", "Y"))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpPGk1YX/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Opened in-memory population 'mammal'
#> Defined genome: 300 loci across 3 chromosomes | chr lengths (Mb): all equal to 100 Mb
#>   Tables written: genome_meta, genome_map, ind_haplotype, ind_genotype, ind_crossover, chr_inheritance, chr_recombination, genome_effects, genome_effect_members, genome_effect_member_origins
#>   Views created: genome_effect_terms, genome_effect_loci
pop <- pop |>
  define_chromosome("X", offspring_sex = "M", from_parent_1 = 0, from_parent_2 = 1) |>
  define_chromosome("Y", offspring_sex = "M", from_parent_1 = 1, from_parent_2 = 0) |>
  define_chromosome("Y", offspring_sex = "F", from_parent_1 = 0, from_parent_2 = 0) |>
  define_chromosome("Y", recombines = FALSE)
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'X' (offspring_sex=M, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=0, from_parent_2=1
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'Y' (offspring_sex=M, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=1, from_parent_2=0
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'Y' (offspring_sex=F, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=0, from_parent_2=0
#> Defined chr_recombination rule for 'Y' (parent_sex=NULL, line_name=NULL): recombines=FALSE
get_table(pop, "chr_inheritance")
#> <tidybreed_table: chr_inheritance>  [6 rows × 5 fields]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   chr_name offspring_sex line_name from_parent_1 from_parent_2
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <chr>             <int>         <int>
#> 1 1        NA            NA                    1             1
#> 2 X        NA            NA                    1             1
#> 3 Y        NA            NA                    1             1
#> 4 X        M             NA                    0             1
#> 5 Y        M             NA                    1             0
#> 6 Y        F             NA                    0             0

# Founders are written with those rules: a male has one X copy and one Y
set.seed(1)
pop <- pop |> define_founder_haplotypes(n_haplotypes = 40)
#> Generating 40 founder haplotypes (method = "uniform")...
#>   Created founder_haplotypes (40 haplotypes x 300 loci)
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("founder_haplotypes") |>
  add_founders(n_males = 2, n_females = 2, line_name = "A")
#> Added 4 founders (2 males, 2 females) to line 'A'
close_pop(pop)

# Avian Z and W: females (ZW) are the heterogametic sex
pop <- open_pop(pop_name = "chicken", db_name = ":memory:") |>
  define_genome(n_loci = 300, n_chr = 3, chr_len_Mb = 100,
                chr_names = c("1", "Z", "W"))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpPGk1YX/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Opened in-memory population 'chicken'
#> Defined genome: 300 loci across 3 chromosomes | chr lengths (Mb): all equal to 100 Mb
#>   Tables written: genome_meta, genome_map, ind_haplotype, ind_genotype, ind_crossover, chr_inheritance, chr_recombination, genome_effects, genome_effect_members, genome_effect_member_origins
#>   Views created: genome_effect_terms, genome_effect_loci
pop <- pop |>
  define_chromosome("Z", offspring_sex = "F", from_parent_1 = 1, from_parent_2 = 0) |>
  define_chromosome("W", offspring_sex = "F", from_parent_1 = 0, from_parent_2 = 1) |>
  define_chromosome("W", offspring_sex = "M", from_parent_1 = 0, from_parent_2 = 0) |>
  define_chromosome("W", recombines = FALSE)
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'Z' (offspring_sex=F, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=1, from_parent_2=0
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'W' (offspring_sex=F, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=0, from_parent_2=1
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'W' (offspring_sex=M, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=0, from_parent_2=0
#> Defined chr_recombination rule for 'W' (parent_sex=NULL, line_name=NULL): recombines=FALSE
close_pop(pop)

# Mitochondria: one maternal copy in both sexes, never recombining
pop <- open_pop(pop_name = "mito", db_name = ":memory:") |>
  define_genome(n_loci = 200, n_chr = 2, chr_len_Mb = c(100, 0.02),
                chr_names = c("1", "MT"))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpPGk1YX/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Opened in-memory population 'mito'
#> Defined genome: 200 loci across 2 chromosomes | chr lengths (Mb): 1:100, MT:0.02
#>   Tables written: genome_meta, genome_map, ind_haplotype, ind_genotype, ind_crossover, chr_inheritance, chr_recombination, genome_effects, genome_effect_members, genome_effect_member_origins
#>   Views created: genome_effect_terms, genome_effect_loci
pop <- pop |>
  define_chromosome("MT", from_parent_1 = 0, from_parent_2 = 1) |>
  define_chromosome("MT", recombines = FALSE)
#> Defined chr_inheritance rule for 'MT' (offspring_sex=NULL, line_name=NULL): from_parent_1=0, from_parent_2=1
#> Defined chr_recombination rule for 'MT' (parent_sex=NULL, line_name=NULL): recombines=FALSE
close_pop(pop)
